title: A Study of Multiplexed PET Imaging in People With Thyroid Cancer
summary:
The researchers are doing this study to see if a type of imaging called "multiplexed positron emission tomography" (mPET) can be used to examine, evaluate, and provide information about tumors in people with thyroid cancer. The researchers will compare the results of mPET imaging to standard PET imaging using the same radiotracers.

mPET imaging is a type of PET scan that can obtain imaging of 2-4 radiotracers at the same time. Standard PET scans can only obtain imaging of 1 radiotracer at a time (such as an 18F-FDG scan or an 124I scan). The researchers think that mPET may be a better way to image cancer because it will allow researchers to see multiple radiotracers on the same images and will reduce the number of scans needed to obtain the images.
criteria:
Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18
* Patients must have pathologically confirmed thyroid cancer and be eligible and scheduled for radioiodine therapy at MSKCC.
* Patient scheduled for standard of care 18F-FDG diagnostic PET and consented to IRB# 18-253 to receive investigational 124I dosimetry PET scan
* For patients with known HIV, HBV, and/or HCV infection \[HIV, HBV, and HCV testing do not need to be performed as part of the study; the below language provides guidelines for inclusivity of patients with known HIV, HBV, and/or HCV infection\]:

  * HIV-infected patients on effective anti-retroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible for this trial.
  * For patients with evidence of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, the HBV viral load must be undetectable on suppressive therapy, if indicated.
  * Patients with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection must have been treated and cured. For patients with HCV infection who are currently on treatment, they are eligible if they have an undetectable HCV viral load.
* Contraception

  o The effects of radiotracers on the developing human fetus are unknown. For this reason and because radiotracers as well as other therapeutic agents used in this trial are known to be teratogenic, participants of child-bearing potential must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) during study therapy and for 6 months following the completion of study therapy (males for 4 months). Should a participant become pregnant or suspect pregnancy while participating in this study, they should inform their treating physician immediately.
* Able to adhere to radiation safety guidelines
* Not pregnant or breastfeeding
* Not experiencing vomiting or diarrhea
* Not taking ongoing anti-thyroid medication
* Does not have non-accumulating/de-differentiated thyroid cancer or RAI-refractive disease
* Has not received a contrast-enhanced CT scan within the last two months
